root_cause.text: During read-only mount with norecovery or disable_roll_forward options, the positive return value from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() (indicating recovered fsync data) was not reset to zero, causing the mount to return a positive error to vfs_get_tree() and triggering a kernel BUG.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the handling of `err > 0` from only setting `-EINVAL` for read-write mounts to also explicitly setting `err = 0` for read-only mounts, preventing the positive value from propagating. The CVE description confirms: "the root cause is we missed to handle error number returned from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() when mounting image w/ ro,norecovery or ro,disable_roll_forward mount option, result in returning a positive error number to vfs_get_tree()". The panic output shows "Filesystem f2fs get_tree() didn't set fc->root, returned 1".

This condition only handles the case when the filesystem is not read-only. For read-only mounts, the condition is false, so the positive err from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() is left unchanged and not reset to zero, leading to the vulnerability.
This statement sets err to a negative value only when the condition (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0) is true. For read-only mounts, it is never executed, so the positive err persists.
